title: Grounded Workflows & Decomposition
description: Study evidence-grounded summarization, extract then transform, decompose complex tasks with checks, and request concise verifiable justification. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Evidence-grounded summarization
lessons.conceptOverview: Require summaries to preserve source meaning and distinguish claims from interpretation. Citation requirements help auditability only when the cited passage actually supports the statement.
lessons.whyItMatters: Citations must support the associated claim.

lessons.title: Extract then transform
lessons.description: Add a source check before applying the conversion.
lessons.conceptOverview: Separate evidence extraction from formatting or synthesis when it makes validation easier. Preserve source spans so transformations can be checked against the original, and avoid treating intermediate outputs as infallible.
lessons.whyItMatters: A correct transformation cannot repair incorrect extracted input.

lessons.title: Decompose complex tasks with checks
lessons.description: Add a relevance gate before summarization.
lessons.conceptOverview: Break multi-part tasks into bounded stages with explicit inputs and outputs. Verify intermediate results when possible, because errors can propagate through a fluent final response.

lessons.title: Request concise verifiable justification
lessons.description: Define a justification format centered on evidence and validation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Ask for assumptions, evidence and decisive checks that help a reader assess the result. Verbosity and elaborate reasoning-like prose are not reliable measures of correctness.
lessons.whyItMatters: Useful justification is checkable rather than merely lengthy.
